chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hassan Musa (peace be upon him) about qiyas (analogical reasoning),
so he said: 'What have you to do with qiyas? Indeed, God will not be asked how He made things permissible or how He made things forbidden.'

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: made permissible (halal) — an act of divine legislation exclusive to God; the Imam's point is that God's methodology of permitting is beyond human inquiry
key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: qiyas — analogical reasoning; a jurisprudential method of deriving new rulings by analogy with existing ones, consistently rejected by the Shia Imams as a valid source of law
key_terms.حَرَّمَ: made forbidden (haram) — an act of divine prohibition exclusive to God; humans cannot replicate God's legislative act through analogy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) say about qiyas (analogical reasoning) in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Uthman ibn Isa, a companion of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), reports asking the Imam about the legitimacy of qiyas as a method in Islamic jurisprudence. The Imam emphatically rejects it by invoking divine sovereignty: just as God is not accountable to creation for His rulings on what is halal and haram, humans have no authority to extend or derive rulings through analogical reasoning.
word_analysis: to you all / have you to do
